subject: Acme - Post-call: GDPR / DPA / SCC selection and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Johnson <laura.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-02T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Acme - Post-call: GDPR / DPA / SCC selection and next steps

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we're aligned: 

Summary
- Use case: ACME will use Redwood inference to power in-app summarization for customer support transcripts.
- Data sensitivity: contains customer PII; ACME indicated some transcripts may include identifiers and potential limited health information in a subset of workflows.
- Timeline: Pilot in Jan, production targeted Q2.

Questions / action items from ACME (your asks)
1) Provide a Data Processing Addendum (DPA) and advise SCC module selection for EU transfers.
2) Confirm Redwood's SOC 2 status and provide attestation.
3) Complete ACME vendor security questionnaire.
4) Clarify controller vs processor roles and subprocessors list.

Our proposed next steps
- Attached: Redwood_DPA_v1.pdf and SCC-selection-matrix.xlsx (initial recommendation).
- We propose Redwood acts as Processor for ACME's use of the API and recommend the controller-to-processor SCC module (see attached matrix).
- Rishi / Neha to coordinate on the vendor security questionnaire; Neha will be point for technical security Qs.
- Vivek (legal) to provide a redlined DPA and confirm SCC approach.
- Schedule 30-min follow-up next Tue to review redlines and timeline.

Could you confirm:
- Who on the ACME side is the DPO or security lead for completion of the questionnaire and DPA?
- Any additional compliance needs (HIPAA / BAA) beyond what we discussed?

Thanks, I'll leave Rishi/Neha/Vivek in to handle the security/legal specifics.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123
[Attachment: Redwood_DPA_v1.pdf]
[Attachment: SCC-selection-matrix.xlsx]

From: Laura Johnson <laura.johnson@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tim Owen <tim.owen@acme.com>, Mike Harris <mike.harris@acme-sec.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T11:10:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Acme - Post-call: GDPR / DPA / SCC selection and next steps

Hi Marissa,

Appreciate the recap — helpful. A few immediate items from our side: 

1) Vendor questionnaire: attached (vendor-security-questionnaire_ACME.docx). Can you have your security team fill this out? We typically need the completed form back within 7 business days for pilots.
2) SOC 2: please send whatever you can share (attestation or SOC 2 report redacted).
3) DPA / SCC: we prefer controller-to-processor wording. Please confirm Redwood's subprocessors and whether you support Data Subject Request (DSR) coordination.
4) HIPAA: some pilot data could be PHI. Do you support HIPAA contracts / BAA? If not, we need to scope pilot data accordingly.

I've looped in Tim (Legal) and Mike (Security), they'll own the questionnaire and legal review. We can aim to review your redline within 3 business days of receiving it.

Thanks,
Laura
Director of Platform Security | Acme Corp
laura.johnson@acme.com
[Attachment: vendor-security-questionnaire_ACME.docx]

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-02T15:45:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Acme - Post-call: GDPR / DPA / SCC selection and next steps

Marissa / Neha / Vivek,

Forwarding Laura's responses. Quick notes from an SE perspective: 
- SOC 2: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II (available to share under NDA); I'll attach the attestation and summary of controls.
- SCC selection: given ACME is a controller and Redwood will process transcripts on behalf of ACME, the controller-to-processor SCC set (Module 2 in our SCC matrix) is the appropriate choice. The DPA should reflect Processor obligations (data retention, deletion on request, subprocessors, security controls).
- HIPAA / BAA: Redwood has a HIPAA-compliant offering for dedicated/private deployments; hosted API may require additional contractual controls. If ACME expects PHI in hosted pilot, legal will need to confirm BAA scope.
- Vendor questionnaire: Neha to own completion; I suggest we pre-fill existing controls and attach SOC 2 / encryption docs.

Neha, can you pick this up and target a completed questionnaire by EOD next Tue? Vivek, can you draft DPA redlines that call out processor role and include subprocessors appendix?

Thanks,
Rishi
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redwood_SOC2_summary.pdf]

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-03T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Acme - Post-call: GDPR / DPA / SCC selection and next steps

Team,

I've drafted a redlined DPA (attached: Redwood_DPA_v2_redlined.pdf) and included a recommended SCC selection: controller-to-processor module (per Rishi). Key points: 
- Redwood confirms role: Processor (we process ACME data strictly per documented instructions).
- Proposed changes: stronger deletion/return obligations on contract expiration, a subprocessors appendix with notice timelines, and a DSR cooperation clause.
- HIPAA / BAA: we can support a BAA but need to lock the deployment model (hosted vs dedicated). Recommend we flag this to Laura/Tim as a potential gating item for the pilot.

Neha, please coordinate on the security questionnaire and attach SOC 2 and encryption/pen-test artifacts. Marissa, once ACME confirms DPO / legal contact, send Vivek any ACME-specific redlines and we'll aim to turn around within 48 hours.

Vivek Kulkarni
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
